body:
# submission name:
frontier_study

# upload zipped `archive.zip`
https://github.com/InfamousBolt/comma_video_compression_challenge/releases/download/frontier-study/archive.zip

(`curl -L` works on that URL.)

# report.txt
```
=== Evaluation results over 600 samples ===
  Average PoseNet Distortion: 0.00003367
  Average SegNet Distortion: 0.00058393
  Submission file size: 178,850 bytes
  Original uncompressed size: 37,545,489 bytes
  Compression Rate: 0.00476355
  Final score: 100*segnet_dist + √(10*posenet_dist) + 25*rate = 0.20
```

# does your submission require gpu for evaluation (inflation)?
no — inflation is CPU-only (torch + brotli).

# did you include the compression script? and want it to be merged?
yes — `compress.sh` / `compress.py` reproduce `archive.zip` from the open, attributed weights (no training).

# is this submission competitive or innovative? explain why
**Neither — and I want to be upfront about that.** This is a **write-up / negative-results
submission** (the challenge lists a "best write-up" prize). It does **not** beat the
leaderboard: the shipped archive is a *fully-attributed reproduction* of the open HNeRV
decoder (CPU score **0.20**, vs the current #1's 0.192), included only so the submission
runs end-to-end via the standard `evaluate.sh`.

Its value is the analysis in [`WRITEUP.md`](submissions/frontier_study/WRITEUP.md): a
quantified explanation of **why the top cluster (0.192–0.199) is a saturated Pareto
frontier**, so others don't re-walk the dead ends.

- **Score budget:** ~62% of the top score is archive size; the HNeRV decoder weights are
  ~93% of the archive. So "beat the top" ≈ "shrink decoder weight bits at equal distortion".
- **Four dead ends, each with data + mechanism:**
  1. *Sub-int8 quantization* — catch-22: per-tensor distortion explodes (6-bit→0.39,
     5-bit→0.70); per-channel halves distortion but won't compress (archive unchanged).
  2. *Per-pair scorer-exploit* — a 65-mode rate-free **oracle** only reaches distortion
     0.0739 ≈ the #1's 0.073; SegNet disagreements are local and unreachable by cheap
     global per-frame perturbations.
  3. *Smaller decoder via distillation* — capacity wall (validated by a C=36 control that
     reproduces the teacher exactly at L1=0).
  4. *Weight palettization* — weights use ~150 distinct int8 values/tensor; int8+brotli is
     already at the entropy floor.
- **The one path with real upside:** from-scratch architecture search trained directly
  against the frozen scorer (real GPU-hours) — i.e. what the leaders did.

A faithful in-process scorer (~1 min vs ~15) and two self-contained Colab notebooks to
reproduce the experiments are in `submissions/frontier_study/study/`.

# additional comments
The decoder weights are **byte-identical to PR #95** (@AaronLeslie138), recovered from PR
#110's public release; no new model was trained (the same reuse-with-attribution pattern
as the current #1). Full attribution in the submission README/WRITEUP.

comments.body:
Thanks for the submission @InfamousBolt! 🤏

A maintainer will review your PR shortly.

To run the evaluation, a maintainer will trigger the `eval` workflow with your PR number.

A few comments: 
- this write up only reports on 4 negative experiments
- all the experiments only used the off-the-shelf trained HNeRV model with no further changes, besides 3.3 which tried to distilled it
- the fact that these 4 experiments did not improve the score does not mean that the "The comma video-compression leaderboard's top cluster (0.192–0.199) is a genuinely *saturated Pareto frontier*"

Given this: 
- I am happy to merge the write-up as a negative experiment report, but only if you fix the conclusion
- No need to have the code here but the description of the experiments have to be improved
- The best write-up award has already been awarded to #95

Closing for now until further updates.

title: frontier_study: why the 0.192 compression frontier is saturated (write-up + reproducible study)
